title: Latency regression rollback plan + customer handshake

Discussed root cause (autoscaler config + batch sizing skew), quick rollback plan, canary strategy, telemetry gaps, and customer communication. Agreed owners and short deadlines for rollback validation, dashboards, and runbook updates.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-14 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Arjun, Sasha, Tom / Liam, Priya, Zoe, Ethan

Summary (auto): quick sync to finalize rollback path and owners after the latency regression on 2026-02-12. Conversation included tradeoffs for immediate rollback vs configuration hotfix, and next steps for customer communication and telemetry.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining on short notice, trying to keep this tight, we got about 45 minutes of content plus Q&A. quick rollcall?
[00:08] Liam O'Keefe: Liam here, sorry for the late ping, been fielding ops alerts.
[00:11] Priya Raman: Priya, SRE lead.
[00:13] Zoe Martinez: Zoe, product - I have notes on impacted flows.
[00:16] Arjun Patel: Arjun from Redwood SE, I looked through traces overnight.
[00:19] Maya Chen: Sasha and Tom on deck for the support and comms side.

[03:02] Arjun: quick re-cap, top line: on the 12th we saw tail latency climb in production across the recommendation endpoint, the proximate cause seems to be an autoscaler policy bump combined with skewed batching. a subset of shards started to queue because batch sizing grew for long sequences. that amplified kv cache misses and queueing.
[03:34] Priya: couple things I'm still fuzzy on - you said "kv cash" earlier in the doc, is that the same as our KV cache layer? some of our telemetry shows lots of gc churn around those pods.
[03:46] Arjun: yeah kv cache, sorry the transcription sometimes flips that. the main sign was increased eviction which increased cold kv lookups and that in turn made per-token lat higher. also the autoscaler had its target concurrency set higher than intended after the config tidying on the 11th.

[07:28] Ethan: to clarify, was this tied to a model switch? we had a small rollout of a larger context model last week.
[07:34] Arjun: good q, we were still on the same model binary. it was the batching heuristics + the autoscaler ceiling that created a hot-path microburst. model change would have been a separate vector.

[10:00] Zoe: customers are asking why the latency doubled for low-latency routes, they see timeouts in their RPS, what's the fastest path for us to restore baseline?
[10:12] Maya: two choices: immediate rollback of the autoscaler/runtime config to previous stable values (fast, but must be validated), or a targeted config guard - cap batch_size and put conservative autoscale ceilings (safer but requires monitoring). rollback gives fastest remediation.

[12:45] Priya: rollback risk is if we flip back and the underlying pressure is still there, we'll see repeated churn, esp during peak. we need a canary window with clear SLO/rollback criteria.
[13:02] Arjun: agree. propose: validate rollback script in staging, run a 10% canary on non-critical tenant traffic for 30 minutes, look at p99 and queue length and kv eviction rate. if metrics look good, escalate to 50% then full. rollback criteria are: p99 < 200ms and queue length stable < threshold and no sustained KV eviction increase.

[17:50] Tom Ruiz: I'll run the rollback script in staging, but note our staging environment doesn't capture the exact traffic distribution - need flamegraphs from prod to validate hypothesis.
[18:05] Arjun: yes flamegraphs please, we need call stacks for the hot shards, I've already instrumented a couple of probes but full traces will help.
[20:30] Liam: what's the customer-facing timeline? our legal folks are pressuring for an SLA note.
[20:38] Maya: we'll send a short incident note by EOD tomorrow with what we know, what we're doing, expected timeline for rollback validation and follow-up. that's in action items.

[23:12] Zoe: is there any security or data residency impact here? some of our orgs flagged audit logs not being present for the period.
[23:19] Sasha Ivanov: not that we've found — logs exist but retention/aggregation for that window had a downstream issue in our ingestion pipeline. we'll include a log snapshot in the incident pack.

[26:45] Priya: what monitoring gaps led to delayed detection? our alerting wasn't tripped until 3 minutes in, can we get earlier signal?
[26:52] Arjun: two gaps: we lack per-shard queue depth metrics surfaced in the main dashboard, and KV eviction rate was only in a debug dashboard. we'll add a derived metric (queue_depth_exposed) and a threshold alert.

[30:05] Ethan: are we considering per-tenant throttles as a long term mitigation? that would limit blast radius.
[30:12] Arjun: yes longer-term mitigations discussed: per-tenant soft throttles, a fallback to a smaller context model when queue depth spikes, and more conservative batching heuristics for tail traffic.

[33:22] Maya: recapping immediate plan: 1) Tom validates rollback script in staging and runs a 10% canary on noncritical tenants, 2) Arjun and Priya exchange flamegraphs and traffic samples, 3) Maya drafts the incident note, 4) Sasha collects logs and prepares audit snapshot. owners as noted in action items.

[36:40] Priya: one operational ask — can you provide a short runbook snippet we can consume into our on-call rotation? specifically exact commands to run rollback and verification steps.
[36:50] Tom: yes we'll produce a minimalized runbook snippet and attach it to the ticket.

[39:10] Zoe: any downstream product fixes needed? for example retry logic in our SDK triggered by timeouts. we want to avoid cascading retries.
[39:20] Maya: recommend temporary client-side backoff parameters; we'll include suggested backoffs in the incident note and coordinate with your SDK owners.

[42:00] Liam: curious on cost impact — did autoscaler overshoot cause cost spike?
[42:05] Arjun: brief blip in infra cost — because concurrency target was higher, we saw more pods and longer-lived batches, but cost delta was small compared to customer impact, we'll include the numbers in the follow-up.

[45:30] Zoe: when is the follow-up meeting?
[45:34] Maya: proposed 2026-02-18 15:00 UTC. 30 minutes, we review flamegraphs and decide permanent mitigations.

[47:50] Priya: one more item — can we get a pre-signed link to the rollback artifacts and script for our security team to review?
[47:58] Tom: yes I'll upload the rollback artifacts to the secure bucket and share the pre-signed URL with the access scope.

[50:15] Arjun: quick note on regressions: we'll also run a small offline stress harness that mimics the long-sequence workload to ensure batch heuristic change won't regress other flows.

[52:48] Maya: ok, thanks everyone. action items and owners in the meeting note. we'll send incident draft and staging validation results as soon as available.
[53:05] Liam: appreciate the quick coordination, talk soon.
[53:10] Meeting end."
